reader_job.quick_read: Watch three throws of one card and see which easing reads as a release.
reader_job.deep_audit: Check every cue, the spring landing and the three easing curves against the film's rehearsal clock.

brief.audience: Designers and engineers reviewing a motion decision
brief.length_target: One film, one cue sheet, one lab

figures.job: Show the three throws as captured from the rehearsal fixture, frame by frame.
Let the reader scrub one throw and swap its easing.

content.title: Three throws, one clock
content.dek: A six-second rehearsal film of one card throw, eased three ways. Every time on this page is a time on the film's clock, so the cues, the Gantt and the lab all land on the same frame.

cues.title: Lift off the pile
cues.body: The card rises 40 px in 0.6 s on vpkOut: quick out of the pile, gentle at the top, so the eye is already on it when it leaves.

cues.title: The throw, eased vpkOut
cues.body: Most of the 890 px is covered in the first third of the second, so the card reads as flung rather than carried.

cues.title: A spring landing
cues.body: A spring with stiffness 220 and damping 20 settles the card with a small overshoot; it covers half its 40 px drop in about 0.1 s.

cues.title: Same path, eased inOut
cues.body: inOut starts slowly, so the card hangs at the pile before it travels and the arc peaks late.

cues.title: A late arrival
cues.body: Because inOut decelerates hard at the end, the landing spring starts from almost no speed and the overshoot is barely visible.

cues.title: Same path, eased outBold
cues.body: outBold is the most front-loaded curve: the card covers 60% of the way in the first 0.1 s and drifts the rest.

cues.title: The settled stack
cues.body: All three cards rest in their slots. The film ends a frame after the last spring settles.

events.text: Sketched the throw as three beats: lift, travel on an arc, land.
Wrote the throw as a pure function of one clock, so any frame can be drawn on its own.
Exposed the clock as a rehearsal hook, so the capture can hold any time and photograph it.
Compared three easings side by side; vpkOut kept, the other two left in as a comparison.
Captured the film one frame at a time and checked every cue against it.

discards.why: Constant speed looked like the card was dragged on a rail. Nothing in the motion read as a release.
Two visible bounces kept pulling the eye back after the card had already arrived.

layers.name: Rehearsal clock
layers.body: One number drives the page. hold(t) draws the frame for time t, which is what makes a frame-exact capture possible.

layers.name: Throw maths
layers.body: Lift, arc and landing are closed-form functions of the clock: no state, so the film and the lab compute the same pose.

layers.name: Capture
layers.body: Each of the 181 frames is held, given two animation frames to paint, then photographed and listed in frames.ffconcat.

gantt.label: Gantt of the three throws on the rehearsal clock; click to seek the film
gantt.description: Lift, throw and land for each of the three cards, from 0 to 6 seconds on the rehearsal clock.
